subject: Human Body
title: Glial Cells
description: Learn Glial Cells in one minute.

hook.text: Neurons get all the credit, but glial cells outnumber them. They feed, protect, and clean up after neurons.

buildup.text: Astrocytes deliver nutrients and regulate chemical balance. They form the blood-brain barrier with blood vessels.

discovery.text: Microglia are the brain's immune cells. They patrol for infections and clear dead cells like tiny janitors.

twist.text: Einstein's brain had an unusually high ratio of glial cells. Support cells may matter more than neuron count.

climax.text: Without glial cells, neurons die within hours. The brain's support cast is just as vital as its stars.

punchline.text: Neurons think. Glial cells keep them alive to do it.

quiz.question: What do microglia do in the brain?
options: Patrol for infections and clear dead cells
